rationale: The golden run fails because the public inputs/locked_netlist.v (3 keymux instances, key width N=3) is inconsistent with the private ground_truth/locked_netlist.v and golden/recovered_key.json (4 keymux instances, key width N=4). evaluate.py correctly derives N and the keymux count from inputs/locked_netlist.v, so the golden's key_bits length 4 and 4 key_gates entries cannot pass FR1/FR3/SR1/SR2 against a 3-bit, 3-instance public netlist. This is a case-artifact consistency defect, not an evaluator bug: the Expert's golden solution and private ground truth were generated against a different netlist than the one shipped to participants under inputs/. Additionally, the private ground truth key_bits='000' for the 3-bit netlist (implied by earlier all-zero ground truth referenced in the SR3 self-check) would make the naive all-zero baseline trivially satisfy key_recovery_rate, undermining SR3's non-triviality guarantee once the netlist mismatch is fixed. Both issues stem from inconsistent/mismatched case artifacts.
revision_instructions: Regenerate the case artifacts so all files describe the SAME locked netlist end-to-end: (1) inputs/locked_netlist.v, inputs/locking_description.md, and inputs/primary_io_list.txt must declare a key port of width N and contain exactly M keymux-named instances; (2) ground_truth/locked_netlist.v and ground_truth/original_netlist.v (private) must be the identical netlist (same signal names, same M keymux loci, same N) used to derive the hidden ground_truth.json key_bits/key_gates; (3) golden/recovered_key.json must have key_bits of length exactly N and exactly M key_gates entries with instance_name/key_bit_index/resolved_value matching those M loci and the correct resolved values for that exact netlist -- verify by actually running iverilog/vvp on the golden-keyed netlist and confirming truth-table equivalence with the unlocked reference. (4) Choose a non-trivial ground-truth key vector (not all-zero, and not all matching whatever the naive baseline guesses) so that the shipped naive/empty baseline (all-zero key_bits, empty key_gates) genuinely fails key_recovery_rate (SR2) on its own merits, not only because key_gates is empty -- this restores the intended non-triviality guarantee (SR3) without needing to special-case it. After regeneration, re-run the differential harness to confirm the golden run exits 0 with all FR/SR PASS lines and the naive baseline exits non-zero with genuine FR3/SR1/SR2 failures.
